instruction:
GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Revit graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, Dynamo, pyRevit, macros, external API automation, Python, or any helper script/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only Revit native GUI tools, menus, dialogs, schedules, sheets, and built-in export commands. Open the provided init.ifc from C:\Users\user\Desktop\init.ifc in Revit before editing, and use init_sheet.png as the local visual reference. Modify the starting model into a two-storey warehouse upgrade scheme with a rectangular 24.0 m by 16.0 m footprint near the project origin. The exterior wall envelope should rise about 6.2 m and include ground and mezzanine slabs; keep the scheme as a roofless, doorless, windowless shell unless needed for Revit editing. Save the deliverables on the Desktop using the exact filenames required below.

The IFC export must use the IFC4 schema, have unique GlobalId values for all IfcRoot objects, and contain one IfcProject, one IfcSite, one IfcBuilding, two IfcBuildingStorey entities, two IfcSpace entities, eight IfcWall entities, and two IfcSlab entities. Do not include IfcRoof, IfcDoor, IfcWindow, IfcStair, IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcCurtainWall, or IfcBuildingElementProxy entities. Name the spaces so the normalized IfcSpace names include Warehouse and Area. Export a one-page Revit sheet PDF named result.pdf; its sheet text must include WAREHOUSE UPGRADE and Principal upgrade sheet. The required BIM categories must be exported as real IFC building elements/spaces, not visual-only placeholders or proxy geometry. Coordinate placement, relationship entities, GUID values, Revit type names, materials, property sets, and harmless extra metadata may vary as long as the stated model geometry, element categories, space names, schedules, sheets, and file outputs are satisfied.
